prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot to Shore Control Room), Main Transformer, export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory when capability<dispatch target; applies accepted ceiling). Public grid, port out of scope. Personnel keep safety authority. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; blocks protection conflicts; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms to Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace). Substation Operator: switching, clearances; modes Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint. Grid Dispatcher: targets. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Alarms safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; Session Revocation Receipt to Cybersecurity Gateway), Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; holds last validated limit on grid comms loss), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale; repair prioritization from severity, growth, weather, production; shows task duration, resources, dependencies), Work Permit Portal, Personnel Tracking Console. Weather Service, Metocean Buoy, Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record). Modes: Weather Hold, Vessel Standby. Vessel Master: Transfer Manifest Addendum, Crew Count Correction. Service Operations Vessel: Recovery Basket Load Sheet. Marine Coordinator: personnel accountability, berth occupancy/arrivals/departures view. Field Supervisor: accountability, cyber briefings, confirms close-access findings documented before leaving. Cyber: Cybersecurity Gateway monitors; Cybersecurity Analyst: Firmware Hash Attestation, evidence; isolate only affected connection; recovery after containment; SCADA Engineer validates restoration. Blade: Duty Planner prioritizes, assigns repair window, crews/vessels, updates records, follow-up inspections, checks readiness vs departure window; Blade Specialist classifies from tile image, close-access NDT inspection, defect records (location, size, orientation, cause, confidence, change), cosmetic vs structural, verifies repair acceptance. Close access only after isolation, rotor restraint, access, rescue verified; HSE Officer reviews method first. Storekeeper checks materials/tooling. Repair plans: prep, application, cure, hold points,

New part:
S471: Weather Service forecasts are considered alongside berth availability because port conditions can delay loading or restrict vessel movement.
S472: The Weather Analyst produces the Visibility Confidence Note to summarize confidence in visibility conditions for near-term port and offshore planning.
S473: The Marine Coordinator uses the Berth Slot Confirmation to align an approved vessel arrival with the assigned berth window.
S474: Crew Transfer Vessel calls are coordinated to avoid conflicts at passenger access points and shared loading areas.
S475: Service Operations Vessel calls are planned with regard to draft, mooring requirements, and the time needed to prepare offshore stores.
S476: The Vessel Master confirms practical arrival and departure estimates against the vessel's operating limits.
S477: Port staging areas are reserved for equipment that must be inspected, secured, or transferred before sailing.
S478: The Warehouse System supports cargo preparation so that planned loads can be assembled before the vessel occupies the berth.
S479: The Storekeeper checks that critical spares are available and that packaging is suitable for marine transport.
S480: Work Permit Portal status is reviewed before departure so that required authorizations are not left unresolved at the port.
S481: The HSE Officer checks that access controls, emergency arrangements, and handling precautions are suitable for the planned activity.
S482: Personnel Tracking Console records are reconciled with the approved crew list before personnel board a vessel.
S483: The Marine Coordinator resolves competing berth requests by considering task urgency, vessel compatibility, and the consequences of delay.
S484: When berth capacity is constrained, lower-priority movements may be resequenced while preserving safe rest periods and required inspections.
S485: Fleet Dispatch Console schedules are updated to reflect confirmed changes to vessel availability and offshore task timing.
S486: Turnaround allowances include time to secure returned equipment, report defects, and prepare the vessel for its next assignment.
S487: Actual arrival, departure, and berth-occupancy times are recorded to improve future capacity estimates.
S488: During disruption, the Marine Coordinator reviews safe alternatives such as a later slot, a different suitable berth, or vessel standby.
S489: Coordination decisions and unresolved constraints are retained for operational review and the next planning cycle.
S490: Maintenance begins only after the work scope, access route, and responsible supervisor have been confirmed for the shift.
S491: The Duty Planner checks that the planned task matches the approved work authorization and that required personnel and equipment are available.
S492: The Work Permit Portal produces the Isolation Boundary Sketch.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
